messages:
maya: CI turned red on nightly for runtime tests — intermittent failure in tests/runtime/serve_shutdown_race_v2_test. 3 failures out of 10 reruns, only on linux-amd64 runners. logs: https://redwood-ci/artifacts/1712349999/serve-shutdown.log

sam: can you paste the failing test name + last few log lines?

maya: failing case: test_interleaved_kv_flush (serve_shutdown_race_v2_test)
maya: last lines: ```
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'assertion failed: inflight_retries.is_empty()', runtime/src/serve/connection.rs:412:13
stack backtrace:
  0: std::panicking::begin_panic
  1: runtime::serve::connection::handle_shutdown
  2: runtime::serve::tests::test_interleaved_kv_flush
```

leo: thanks. can you share the exact command you used to rerun locally?

maya: ran: ```bazel test //runtime/tests:serve_shutdown_race_v2_test --test_output=errors --runs_per_test=10```
maya: also tried: ```cargo test --test serve_shutdown_race_v2 -- --nocapture --test-threads=1```

olivia: any test seed or env that made it repro more reliably?

maya: yes — when I set TEST_SEED=84591 it failed ~40% locally. without seed it was ~10%. exec patch that added an extra deferred flush looks suspicious (commit range: a1b2c3d..d4e5f6a).

sam: can someone try a quick bisect across that commit range? might be a single offending change.

jen: I can run a targeted bisect on CI if you give me the two commits. will queue it now.

maya: commit range above. pref test binary with TEST_SEED=84591, RUST_BACKTRACE=1.

ci-bot: queued bisect job #6721 on linux-amd64 pool, will post updates here. :gear: 

leo: small suggestion: try forcing single-threaded runtime for the test (`RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`) — many timing flakes go away. also try disabling prefetch cache to see if interaction with kv flush is the trigger.

olivia: good idea. maya — can you run one CI rerun with RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 and another with PREFETCH_CACHE=0 to see delta?

maya: started both jobs: rerun-1 (single-thread): https://redwood-ci/job/6722, rerun-2 (prefetch off): https://redwood-ci/job/6723

sam: if rerun-2 is green and rerun-1 still flakes, that points at cache timing. if both green — maybe flaky due to scheduling noise.

maya: quick glance: rerun-1 = 1/10 failed, rerun-2 = 0/10 failed so far.

leo: that looks like a caching/timing interaction. can someone add a very small sleep before flush in the test as a quick probe? e.g. `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2)).await` before the flush call to see if it stabilizes.

olivia: if that stabilizes, we should add a short-term guard in code to make flush idempotent rather than test sleep.

maya: added probe sleep and ran locally with TEST_SEED=84591, 0/50 failures so far. pushing a patch to a diagnostic branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/984

sam: great. once bisect finishes we can decide whether to revert or fix properly. thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup:

jen: bisect job #6721 found the culprit: commit d4e5f6a (kv: defer flush until connection close). reporting in CI console now.

maya: perfect — I'll open a PR to make the deferred flush resilient to inflight retries (idempotent flush + guard). linking to PR in a bit.

leo: also add a test harness change to run the flaky test under a smaller-tick tokio scheduler for CI to catch similar timing issues earlier.

olivia: noted for followup — create an issue to add more systematic flaky test wrapping.

maya: thanks team — will update once PR is up and CI is clean.
